## Accession logic

For GEO/SRA, teach the hierarchy:

```text
GSE study -> GSM sample -> SRP project -> SRX experiment -> SRR run
```

ENA and ArrayExpress may provide clearer FASTQ URLs for some datasets. Record the route used.

## ENA route

Use stable HTTPS/FTP links from ENA metadata when available. In the workshop, the ENA table is turned into a small CSV and each URL is downloaded with `curl`:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -w /work \
  docker.io/fgualdr/ngs-curl:latest \
  curl \
  -L URL_TO_FASTQ_GZ \
  -o raw_data/fastq/rnaseq/SAMPLE_R1.fastq.gz
```

## SRA route

SRA Toolkit is useful for future projects that do not provide direct FASTQ URLs. Start from the CSV downloaded from SRA Run Selector and save it as:

```text
raw_data/metadata/SraRunTable.csv
```

The first column is `Run`, for example `SRR13090294`. The optional example below downloads every run listed in that first column:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

csv_file="raw_data/metadata/SraRunTable.csv"
out_dir="raw_data/fastq/sra_example"

mkdir -p "${out_dir}"

if [[ ! -f "${csv_file}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: CSV file not found: ${csv_file}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

tail -n +2 "${csv_file}" | cut -d, -f1 | tr -d '\r' |
while read -r run_accession
do
  [[ -n "${run_accession}" ]] || continue

  echo "Downloading ${run_accession}"
  fasterq-dump "${run_accession}" \
    --split-files \
    --threads 2 \
    --outdir "${out_dir}"

  gzip -f "${out_dir}/${run_accession}"*.fastq
done
```

Run that script inside the SRA Toolkit image:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -w /work \
  docker.io/fgualdr/ngs-sra-tools:latest \
  bash scripts/day1/example_sra_run_selector_download.sh
```

This is an example route, not the main download route for the workshop.

## Reproducibility record

Version the accession table. Do not version downloaded FASTQ files.
